correctness.rationale: The Rule-73 3-bit truth table determines explicit 4- and 16-state de Bruijn constraint graphs. Every cyclic fixed or twice-fixed configuration bijects with a closed walk, including rings shorter than the neighborhood. Exhaustive disjoint-elementary-cycle determinant expansions, independently recalculated by the included exact integer code, give precisely 1-z^3-z^4 and (1-z)^2(1+z^2)^2(1-2z^2-z^3+z^4). Formal log determinants prove the two zeta formulas at all lengths. Verified primitive strongly connected components and exact rational root bounds give simple dominant Perron eigenvalues with alpha>beta, hence the exponential orbit/equilibrium comparison. An independent bit-level checker exhaustively checked all 524,286 indexed states across n=1..18 as a cross-check, not as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Rule 73 is a historically studied elementary nonlinear cellular automaton with locally persistent structures. Its complete all-length period-one/two orbit census and exact rational spatial zeta functions are natural, nontrivial dynamical invariants. An explicit spectral gap alpha in (1.490,1.491) versus beta in (1.220,1.221) proves two-cycles exponentially dominate equilibria, and n=5 demonstrates oscillations with no equilibria. This exact infinite-size theorem offers a useful benchmark for comparing local dynamical rules, beyond an arbitrary finite slice; it makes no unsupported claims about other temporal periods.
